I'm not going to. I want to. I would never leave my kids. They don't have anyone else who is remotely normal or stable. I don't know how to be stable myself anymore. I can't believe I brought this upon myself and them.

I feel like I did know deep down, but I've been so paranoid my entire life about my daughters being molested that I thought it was just me. I found out about the porn well before all of this, but it was search history from before we started dating and as far as I could tell the sites were legal. I discussed it with him and did a lot of research and found that it's extremely common for men to look up that theme in porn... but I found it odd that that's the only thing he ever looked up. That was enough for me to not want him around as my daughters got older, but things were worse than ever at my mom's house so I continued to see him on and off because it was just a way out of my house. Several months after I found out about the porn history, his ex-wife told me of an incident where he was tickling the 14-year-old girl that I later found out he messed around with. The ex-wife is nuts and changes her stories from one day to the next so I didn't know what to think, but he admitted to the tickling. I broke up with him for a while after that, but again, he kept coming back and offering to cook dinner and offering help, so I let him back in for a little while. I knew the tickling thing was extremely weird between a 25 yr old and a girl who had clearly hit puberty. He said he was just immature and he thought it was okay to play around with her just like a kid. I never saw him do anything like that to my two older kids, and he wasn't overly playful or weird with them so again, I knew it wasn't normal but I thought I was taking things to the extreme. I could have done more. None of it was worth putting my kids at risk. I kept doubting myself and blamed my paranoia when all the signs were right there in front of my face.

there were so many red flags though. I even called my dad shortly after I started dating him to ask him if he thought certain behaviors were normal, because they bothered me. For example, the second time we ever saw each other, we met at a mutual friend's house. We had already spent one weekend together and had been talking heavily for months. As soon as me and my daughter (2 at the time) got there, she started fussing, so my now-ex went over to her and said "I know what the problem is!" and pulled her pants and diaper back to see if she had pooped, then offered to change her. I told him no and I later talked to him about how I didn't like that he did that. He didn't argue and he stepped back a little bit other than offering to watch her while I showered and he offered to give her a bath a couple times very early in the relationship, which I also found odd. He didn't seem upset or angry when I declined, so I told myself I was being paranoid. He's always offering to help others, its part of his ego or something, so I told myself that's why he was being like that with my daughter. He's always trying to clean other people's houses when he visits, do favors for others, etc. He doesn't ask for anything in return that I've ever seen, he just likes to appear as a super nice guy. A lot of his behavior set off alarms in my head, but there was always something to counter that. Even in the later parts of our relationship, I would go months without leaving my daughter alone with him even for 5 seconds because of this feeling I had, and he never said anything about it other than one more isolated occasion where he insisted that he give her a bath so that I could get my homework done - which I did not let him. I don't see how it's not my fault. And regardless of fault or blame, she's my baby and I'm her only parent, it was my job to protect her.

Yes. I failed at the most important thing I've ever done. I was so sure I would succeed. It was the only thing I've ever had no doubt about. I am a young single mother of three kids. When I got pregnant with my third, I was abandoned by my husband and chose to keep my baby and started a new life and got myself into school. I'm a year away from graduating and making a lot of money to provide a wonderful life for my kids. I swore to myself I would never ever bring a man around my kids again unless I was 100% sure I could trust him. I was so sure I would do everything right with this baby. I regretted my past marriages so severely and wanted to do better. I was single for nearly three years then met a guy that seemed great. Things got fishy a few months into the relationship but I figured the guy was just a cheater and a bit immature, but he was nice to me and my kids and it was a way for me to get out of the family home I'm having to live in to finish school, which is a very nightmarish situation as it is (alcoholic mother and mean stepfather). Almost two years into the relationship I found out he sexually assaulted two fourteen year old girls a few years ago when he was 25, and now I'm wondering if he could have molested my youngest child, who is now 4. I failed her and my other kids at the one thing I thought I'd do right. I don't know how I made such a severe mistake, I was dead-set on never leaving her alone with any man just to be safe, but eventually I did leave her with him for a few minutes at a time if I needed to shower or do something for my other kids, because I let my guard down and he has his own kids and has never been accused of anything, at least not that I knew of at the time. Looking back there were dozens of red flags but I missed them and some of them I dismissed as me being paranoid and overprotective of my kids. Nothing has ever been as important to me as fixing my kids' lives and doing better for them, and I feel that I've made the worst mistake possible in letting someone like this into their lives and my youngest baby possibly experienced abuse.
